items.followUp: What is a measuring instrument? Describe a measuring tape and state its least count.

rubric.why: States the purpose of a measuring instrument.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that it is a device used to measure physical quantities.

rubric.description: States the length of a meter rod.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is one metre (100 cm) long.

rubric.why: Describes the scale divisions on the meter rod.
rubric.description: States the graduations of a meter rod.
rubric.how: Award for naming its centimetre and millimetre divisions.

rubric.why: Gives the meter rod’s smallest division and least count.
rubric.description: States the least count of a meter rod.
rubric.how: Award for stating that its least count is 1 mm (0.1 cm).

modelAnswer: Devices used to measure physical quantities are called measuring instruments.
A meter rod is a graduated strip 1 m (100 cm) long, used to measure length.
It is marked in centimetres, and each centimetre is divided into millimetres.
Its least count is 1 mm (0.1 cm).

items.followUp: Using a speed–time graph, derive the relation v_f²−v_i²=2as.

rubric.why: Uses the slope of the speed–time graph to relate acceleration, time and speeds.
rubric.description: Obtains the acceleration relation from the graph’s slope.
rubric.how: Award for a correct slope relation.

rubric.why: Uses the area under the speed–time graph as displacement.
rubric.description: Expresses displacement as the graph’s area.
rubric.how: Award for the trapezium-area expression for displacement.

rubric.why: Substitutes the slope relation into the area equation and combines the results.
rubric.description: Combines the graph equations by substitution.
rubric.how: Award for obtaining the product expression for 2as.

rubric.why: Reaches the required relation using the difference of squares.
rubric.how: Award for the correct final relation.

modelAnswer: From the slope of the speed–time graph, a=(V_f−V_i)/t.
The displacement s is the area under the graph: s=½(V_i+V_f)t.

items.followUp: What is zero error? Explain how it affects a measurement.

rubric.why: Identifies the condition that produces zero error.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the instrument gives a non-zero reading when the actual quantity is zero.

rubric.why: Explains that zero error must be corrected to improve the measurement.
rubric.description: States why zero error is accounted for.
rubric.how: Award for saying that a zero correction is applied to the reading to obtain a more accurate measurement.

modelAnswer: Zero error is the non-zero reading shown by an instrument when the quantity being measured is actually zero.
We check for zero error and apply a zero correction to the reading so that the measurement is more accurate.
